ratings_why.fun: Each turn is a real push-your-luck choice with two opposite ways to win, and Tags give a growing board, but several Run prompts a turn could start to feel like a chore.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7: one shared bust gauge across the whole Recruit Phase, where getting Caught is itself a resource (Seized, Tagged, bought back to replay its When played). No current tribe plays like that.

verdict_why: The core reads well and needs no rework; two cards need wording fixes before a player can read them.

points.text: Grisel: say whether the stab is one hit of 3 per Heat or many 3-damage hits, and don't use 'Seized' for an enemy unit. Write 'you get a plain Tagged copy of it in your next shop'.
Creel-Weaver should say, as Gentleman Moss does, whether 'Whenever you Run' cards like Spraint Stone Keeper and Old Wick trigger again on the extra time.
Slipway Champion: write 'Run up to three times, choosing after each roll', so the card reads as a small push-your-luck game of its own.

The fantasy comes through in play: the herons taking the fall, the auction buyback and the near miss at the Limit are all smuggling-ballad beats. A Heat gauge with the Limit marked, plus a customs ghost in a Seized unit's slot, is what makes it readable.

standouts.why: Sergeant Squacco taking the seizure himself turns the comedy pair into a mechanic, and it reads at a glance.
Close-Shave Creeler's double for landing exactly on the Limit is the near miss in one line.
Auctioneer Hackle makes buying your goods back from customs a payoff, which is the seed's best joke.

weakest.why: Lantern Reach Hothead is a plain Heat-to-Attack card that Officer Nyx does better.
Salt-Pan Runner is a plain gold Run with no twist.
Holt Kit's 'every two Runs' growth is small and easy to forget.

flags.note: One hit or many, and 'it is Seized' applied to an enemy unit.
Unclear whether 'Whenever you Run' triggers repeat on the extra Run.
With Bell-Diver Gran and Squacco's reset, Old Wick could buff the board 5 or 6 times a turn.
With Creel-Weaver, Gentleman Moss makes the first Run happen three times; worth checking with Thousand-Channel Pilot.
